limitations_and_boundaries: OFormer generally does not show superiority over other operator learning frameworks for small data regime and problems with relatively smooth target functions.
The paper focuses on standard PDE benchmark problems and does not explore very large-scale or highly chaotic systems.
The computational cost of OFormer is higher than FNO variants in terms of memory and training speed.
The study is limited to the specific PDEs and datasets considered; generalization to other PDEs or real-world applications is not evaluated.

research_questions.statement: Can an attention-based framework (OFormer) effectively learn solution operators for PDEs on both uniform and non-uniform grids, and how does it compare to state-of-the-art operator learning methods?

provenance.text_excerpt: Moreover, our model performs similarly under different resolutions, indicating its robustness to different resolution.

claims.statement: OFormer is robust to different resolutions.

provenance.text_excerpt: As shown in Table 2, equipped with a smooth activation function, FNO+ outperforms all other methods significantly, as the target function u(·, 1) is relatively smooth due to the presence of diffusion term, and has a periodic characteristic in the spatial domain.

claims.statement: FNO+ outperforms all other methods significantly on Burgers' equation due to smooth activation and periodic characteristic.

provenance.text_excerpt: Our framework is built upon self-attention, cross-attention, and a set of point-wise multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), and thus it makes few assumptions on the sampling pattern of the input function or query locations.

claims.statement: OFormer makes few assumptions on the sampling pattern of the input function or query locations.

provenance.text_excerpt: where it is on par with MWT on NS2-full with substantially less parameters.

claims.statement: OFormer has substantially less parameters than MWT while achieving comparable performance on NS2-full.

provenance.text_excerpt: We observe that for small data regime (NS2-part, NS3) and problems with relatively smooth target function (viscid Burgers’, Darcy), OFormer generally does not show superiority over other operator learning-frameworks.

claims.statement: OFormer does not show superiority over other operator learning frameworks for small data regime and smooth target functions.
OFormer's training and inference efficiency is comparable to other models, with 1.89 iters/sec and 2.32 sec inference time.

provenance.text_excerpt: we show that the proposed framework is competitive on standard PDE benchmark problems and can flexibly be adapted to different types of grids.

claims.statement: OFormer can flexibly be adapted to different types of grids.

provenance.text_excerpt: For more complex instances like Navier-Stokes equation, we find that OFormer has strong performance in data sufficient regime, where it is on par with MWT on NS2-full with substantially less parameters.

claims.statement: OFormer has strong performance in data sufficient regime for Navier-Stokes equation.

datasets.description: 1D viscous Burgers' equation on uniform grid; operator maps initial condition to solution at t=1.
datasets.name: Burgers' equation

datasets.description: 2D Darcy flow on uniform grid; operator maps coefficient a to solution u.
datasets.name: Darcy flow

datasets.description: 2D Navier-Stokes with ν=1e-4, T=30, small data regime.
datasets.name: Navier-Stokes NS2-part

datasets.description: 2D Navier-Stokes with ν=1e-4, T=30, large data regime.
datasets.name: Navier-Stokes NS2-full

datasets.description: 2D Navier-Stokes with ν~U([0.4,1])e-4, T=30, diverse viscosities.
datasets.name: Navier-Stokes NS-mix

experiments_or_tasks: Compare against FNO, MWT, Galerkin/Fourier Transformer.
Evaluate OFormer on 1D viscous Burgers' equation, 2D Darcy flow, and 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes equation with different viscosities and dataset sizes.

methods.name: OFormer
methods.protocol_description: Attention-based operator learning framework with self-attention, cross-attention, and point-wise MLPs; few assumptions on input sampling pattern or query locations.

methods.name: FNO-2D
methods.protocol_description: Fourier Neural Operator with 2D convolutions; for NS-mix, increased modes to 12 and width to 32.

methods.name: Galerkin Transformer (G.T.)
methods.protocol_description: Galerkin Transformer; for Navier-Stokes, hidden dimension increased from 64 to 96, training epochs extended to 200 (150 on large dataset).

methods.name: FNO+
methods.protocol_description: FNO variant with GELU activation and no normalization.

study_units.name: Benchmark on uniform grid PDEs
